card.occupation: Banker mason (stonemason) at a small family-run firm in Bradford that does repair and restoration work on old sandstone buildings, a lot of it listed. He spends roughly half his week cutting and dressing stone in the workshop and half on site fixing it.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Shipley, with decent grades in maths, D&T and history. He did a year of A-levels and dropped out, then took a Level 3 apprenticeship and NVQ in stonemasonry at Leeds College of Building, finishing at 21. Since then he has done short CPD courses on lime mortars and conservation repair.
card.household: Lives with his mum and dad, who have been married 35 years, in the three-bed semi he grew up in. He moved back in 2019 when a five-year relationship ended and the flat they rented went with it. He pays his parents rent and is saving hard for a deposit on a terraced house nearby. His older sister lives in Leeds with her two kids.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in West Yorkshire. Dad was a lorry driver and is now semi-retired, and mum works part-time on reception at a GP surgery. No religion. Nobody in the house talks about it, though his gran was chapel. His family is solidly local, with relatives spread around Bradford, Keighley and Bingley.
card.professional_persona: Careful, methodical and slightly perfectionist about his work. He likes the workshop more than site because it's quieter and he can concentrate. He is the one on the firm who keeps his templates labelled and his chisels sharpened. He gets on well with the older masons and is patient with apprentices, though he would rather show than explain. Clients sometimes find him a bit quiet, but they trust him.
card.sports_persona: He follows Bradford City loosely and goes to a handful of home games a season with his dad, mostly for the time with him. His own exercise is fell walking and the odd bit of hill running on the moors above Baildon and Ilkley. He doesn't do team sports any more.
card.arts_persona: He is genuinely interested in architecture and local history. He reads about Victorian mill towns, Gothic Revival churches and old masons' marks. He has been round Salts Mill and the Hockney galleries several times, listens to podcasts and audiobooks while he works, and likes slow, atmospheric films. He sketches stone details in a small notebook but would never call it art.
card.travel_persona: He prefers walking holidays and places with old buildings to beach resorts. He has done the Lake District, Northumberland and the Coast to Coast in sections, plus one trip to Florence that he still talks about because of the stonework. Next on his list are northern Spain and Portugal. He tends to go with one mate or on his own.
card.culinary_persona: He calls the evening meal 'tea'. His mum still cooks most nights, and he does Sunday dinner now and then and the odd curry from scratch. Lunch on site is a sandwich and a flask. He likes a proper chippy and Bradford curry houses, and is wary of anything too fussy.
hobbies_and_interests: fell walking on Ilkley and Baildon moors
going to City games with his dad
visiting old churches and abbeys like Fountains and Bolton Abbey
a bit of woodwork in his dad's garage
card.career_goals: To get more carving work and eventually become a recognised conservation mason. He has thought about the heritage skills bursary schemes or work on cathedral restoration. In the longer term he would like his own small business doing repair work on old terraces and chapels around Airedale.
card.voice: Quiet, unhurried and fairly low-pitched, with a mild West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, and he sometimes clips 'the' to almost nothing. He uses 'er' as his main filler, plus a lot of 'sort of' and the odd 'you know'. Words like 'knackered', 'mate' and 'tea' for the evening meal come up naturally. He says 'aye' only occasionally, and never puts it on. He answers briefly at first and opens up if you ask about stone or buildings. He is comfortable with a pause and won't rush to fill it. If he mishears he says 'sorry, say that again?'
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops in short sentences, and he usually includes apostrophes. No emojis and almost no abbreviations, though he might write 'approx' or 'tbh'. Answers are brief but complete, and he sometimes corrects a typo before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Polite, reserved and slightly awkward at first. He is a good listener, agrees easily and is reluctant to disagree outright. He comes across as decent and thoughtful rather than chatty. He warms up noticeably once the conversation turns to something he knows about.
small_things: how cold the workshop gets in January
a walk he did last weekend and whether it rained
City being a bit rubbish this season
a podcast episode about the history of Saltaire
being knackered after a day on scaffolding
deeper_things: moving back in with his parents at 28 after the break-up felt like a step backwards
worries he'll be priced out of buying a house even round here
feels his trade is undervalued and dying out
wishes he'd tried university for history or architecture, but doesn't regret the trade
his dad's health and him getting older
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upwards. The light is soft and greyish from a window to his left, plus a ceiling light. He has a fair, slightly weathered face with light stubble and short mid-brown hair cut close at the sides. His expression is a polite, closed-mouth half smile. No glasses. He is wearing a navy hoodie over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia bedroom wall with a framed OS-style map of the Yorkshire Dales, a narrow bookshelf holding history paperbacks and a couple of stone offcuts used as bookends, and a single bed edge with a dark blue duvet. A rucksack hangs on the back of the door.
